ApprovalStatus.description: Approval state of a decision, criterion or constraint.
ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

Criterion.description: A question an option must satisfy; required criteria gate resolution.

approval_status.description: Where the criterion stands in the human approval track; a generated criterion must enter it.

approved_by.description: Human who approved the criterion; required once it is approved.
approved_by.title: Approved By

decision_basis.description: Optional note on the principle or source behind the criterion; carried for readers, not interpreted by the kernel.
decision_basis.title: Decision Basis

id.description: Stable id that assessments and rankings use to refer to this criterion.
id.title: Id

kind.description: Whether evidence can settle this criterion; Jev classifies it once (kind_source "jev").

kind_source.description: Who set `kind`: None means not classified yet (the decision asks Jev once).
kind_source.title: Kind Source

priority.description: Whether the criterion blocks resolution (required) or only adds weight to the ranking (supporting).

proposal_status.description: Whether the caller supplied the criterion or a generator proposed it, which decides if approval is needed.

proposed_by.description: Actor that proposed the criterion, for accountability.
proposed_by.title: Proposed By

question.description: The question an option must satisfy, answered from evidence or by judgement.
question.title: Question

schema_version.description: Version of this contract's shape, so a reader can reject a payload written for another shape.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

scope.description: Optional note on what the criterion applies to when narrower than the decision; carried for readers, not interpreted by the kernel.
scope.title: Scope

weight_rule.description: Optional note on how the criterion is weighed against others; carried for readers, not interpreted by the kernel.
weight_rule.title: Weight Rule

Criterion.title: Criterion

CriterionKind.description: What can settle a criterion: facts about the world, or a judgement of the designs.
CriterionKind.title: CriterionKind

Option.description: A candidate answer to a decision question.

approval_status.description: Where the option stands in the human approval track; a generated option must enter it.

approved_by.description: Human who approved the option; required once it is approved.
approved_by.title: Approved By

assumptions.description: Premises that must hold for this option to be right, kept verbatim so a reader can challenge them.
assumptions.title: Assumptions

description.description: What choosing this option means in practice, so it can be judged against the criteria.
description.title: Description

id.description: Stable id that criterion assessments and the final selection use to refer to this option.
id.title: Id

named_in_goal.description: A host's claim that the caller's goal names this option; the kernel verifies the wording.
named_in_goal.title: Named In Goal

proposal_status.description: Whether the caller supplied the option or a generator proposed it, which decides if approval is needed.

proposed_by.description: Actor that proposed the option, for accountability.
proposed_by.title: Proposed By

schema_version.description: Version of this contract's shape, so a reader can reject a payload written for another shape.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

source_refs.description: Evidence ids or references this option rests on; grounding checks that generated options cite real evidence.
source_refs.title: Source Refs

title.description: Short name shown to people choosing between options.
title.title: Title

ProposalStatus.title: ProposalStatus

options.description: Candidate options the host generated; every one is a proposal awaiting approval.

proposed_criteria.description: Criteria the host suggests; every one is a proposal awaiting approval.
